title: Safe JSON continuation protocol and backoff policy for truncated structured outputs
creator: Ethan Zhang
description:
Problem: When clients receive truncated or mid-token structured JSON over streaming (chat/complete) and then retry or resume, we see a combination of failures: incompatible escaping heuristics, duplicate tool calls, and non-deterministic repairs across SDKs. This ticket designs and implements a 'Safe JSON Continuation Protocol' and an accompanying client/server backoff/orchestration policy to make retries idempotent and compatible with older SDKs that expect line-delimited JSON or single-object responses.

Goals:
- Provide an explicit minimal wire protocol for continuation that can be implemented as a compatibility shim on the server and in SDK wrappers.
- Ensure tool/function calls are not duplicated on resume by providing deterministic idempotency hints tied to the response stream and model output tokens.
- Define a deterministic escaping / repair strategy for truncated JSON that preserves model intent while preventing parse errors.
- Offer a sensible backoff and retry orchestration to avoid amplifying load during model fallbacks or partial responses.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Server emits a continuation token header when streaming structured outputs might be truncated (e.g., X-JSON-Continuation: <opaque-token>) and documents the semantics.
2) SDKs can resume by supplying the continuation token and optional last-received-fragment checksum; server-side stitch logic produces a single coherent JSON object or an explicit error with repair hints.
3) Tool/function calls invoked by the model in the truncated region are guarded by idempotency markers (tool_call_id) so retries do not re-run side-effects.
4) New escaping rules (deterministic close-sentinel fallback) are implemented and unit-tested across known edge cases: unterminated strings, truncated escape sequences, and partial unicode codepoints.
5) Observability: failure rate and retry amplification are visible in a dashboard; regression threshold set to <=0.5% for high-traffic routes.
6) Backward compatibility shim documented for older SDKs: behavior falls back to LDJSON streaming semantics if continuation token is absent.
implementation_notes:
Design summary: Introduce an opaque 'continuation_token' emitted in response headers for streaming endpoints and also included as a final event in streaming payload when the runtime detects potential truncation risk. Server-side stitcher accepts the token with an optional 'last_fragment_checksum' and attempts: 1) apply deterministic escape repairs, 2) stitch with cached prefix/KV cache, 3) mark any tool calls in the stitched region with tool_call_id and 'may_have_executed' flag.

Idempotency model: tool calls will carry tool_call_id derived from (request_id, model_offset_range, stable_nonce). If a resume arrives with an identical tool_call_id, server returns the previously recorded result instead of re-invoking the integration. We will store short-lived tool call results in a bounded in-memory LRU keyed store with eviction policy tuned per route.

Backoff/orchestration: client retry policy should use exponential backoff with jitter and an initial 300ms base. Server will emit a 'retry-advice' header when rate-limited or when the request hit a fallback model variant.

Compatibility shim: If continuation_token missing, SDKs fall back to LDJSON line-by-line heuristics; an opt-in strict mode will error rather than heuristically repair.

Testing: fuzz truncated Unicode and multi-byte sequences, simulate partial tool call payloads, and run load tests to ensure the LRU size bound prevents memory amplification on hot routes.
comments: 2026-02-18 - Ethan Z.: Initial RFC posted to Confluence. Proposed header: X-JSON-Continuation. Requesting feedback from SDK and runtime teams.

2026-02-22 - Priya M.: Reviewed idempotency approach. Concern: storing tool results in-memory may not work for long-running workflows. Suggest a short TTL + optional durable backing for enterprise routes.

2026-02-25 - Diego F. (runtime): Prototype stitcher implemented; needs deterministic escaping tests. Observed a case where concatenating broke when model emitted an extra '}' inside a string — added heuristics to prefer adding a closing sentinel only outside quoted regions.
2026-03-03 - Priya M.: Added backoff policy details; want to default to client-side exponential jitter and server 'retry-advice' header. Assigned visible dashboard metric owners: infra-observability.
2026-03-08 - QA: Added fuzz test results for truncated UTF-8 sequences. Found a regression in older Node SDK where Buffer slicing produced invalid checksum — opened SDK PR.

2026-03-10 - PM (Marta R.): Confirmed release window api-2026.03 acceptable for limited beta. Need legal sign-off for retaining short-lived tool outputs for idempotency; raised to security/compliance.
notes_for_next_steps:
1) Agree TTL and storage bounds for tool result cache (proposal: 5 minutes default, configurable per route).
2) Implement server header + final-event emission in runtime.
3) Merge SDK resume API and publish compatibility guide.
4) Run canary on low-traffic routes and monitor retry amplification.
5) Follow-up ticket for enterprise durable idempotency store if required.
